```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The Republican Congress and the White House championed the largest expansion in the history of the community health centers program.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Community health centers are locally-controlled, private providers of primary and preventive care services in the most underserved communities in the country.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Community health centers are not federal providers.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Funds are awarded competitively to underserved communities through the federal grant program.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Community health centers provide access to doctors and nurses regardless of a patient's ability to pay.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"One in four children from low-income families receives health care at community health centers.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The President and Congress have already made it possible for community health centers to serve an additional 3 million Americans, for a total of 13 million.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"This is part of the President's five-year plan to fund 1,200 new or expanded sites to serve an additional 6.1 million people.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Today, there are more than 600 new or expanded health centers delivering preventive and primary care to patients in medically underserved communities across America.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Support for plans to continue increasing access to community health centers, so that uninsured and low-income Americans have reliable options for receiving high-quality medical care.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
